questions.question:
The statements below are followed by two conclusions labeled I and II. Assuming that the information in the statements is true, even if it appears at variance with generally established facts, decide which conclusion(s) logically and definitely follow(s) from the information given in the statements.

**Statements:**

All spiders are snails.

All molars are snails.

**Conclusion:**

I. No spider is a molar.

II. Some spiders are molars.

options.text: Either conclusion I or conclusion II follows.

questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• The *neither-nor* case is applicable when both the conclusions are false, whether definite or not.
 
• The *either-or* case is applicable for a pair of statements *only if* either of the following pair of *keywords* is used AND *only if* the following *conditions* are satisfied:

Keywords:

 
• *All* and *some not*
 
• *Some* and *no*

Conditions:

 
• The *same elements* are used in the two conclusions. For example, in this case, the elements *jungles* and *malls* are common to both conclusions.
 
• Both conclusions should be possibilities. That is, they should be *false because the conclusion is possible but not definite*.

Then, the pair of conclusions are considered as *complementary pairs.*

***The least possible Venn diagram is,***__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1efcdd731b0869e489e92cce84ce9ba8afedbe9b4b63e05ab08860f1e62d30dd.png] 

__**Conclusion I:**__ No spider is a molar → False (This is definitely false)

__**Conclusion II: **__Some spiders are molars → False (This is possible but not definite)

__Explanation:__

In the given question, the keywords provided (*Some* and *no*) satisfy the concept of the Either-or case.

Conclusion I and Conclusion II form a complementary pair.

Hence,** “either conclusion I or conclusion II”** follows

questions.question:
Find out the two signs to be interchanged to make the following equation correct.

27 + 27 × 27 − 27 ÷ 27 = −701
questions.solution:
Interchanging the signs and using BODMAS rule,

**Option 1 ****→ – and ×**

The original equation is,

27 + 27 × 27 − 27 ÷ 27 = −701

Interchanging the signs,

27 + 27 – 27 × 27 ÷ 27 = −701

Using BODMAS rule,

27 + 27 – 27 × 1 = - 701

27 + 27 – 27 = - 701

27 is not equal to – 701

**Option 2 ****→ + and ÷**

The original equation is,

27 + 27 × 27 − 27 ÷ 27 = −701

Interchanging the signs,

27 ÷ 27 × 27 – 27 + 27 = - 701

Using BODMAS rule,

1 × 27 – 27 + 27 = - 701

27 – 27 + 27 is not equal to – 701

**Option 3 ****→ – and ÷**

The original equation is,

27 + 27 × 27 − 27 ÷ 27 = −701

Interchanging the signs,

27 + 27 × 27 ÷ 27 – 27 = - 701

Using BODMAS rule,

27 + 27 × 1 – 27 = - 701

27 + 27 – 27 is not equal to – 701

**Option 4 ****→ × and ÷**

The original equation is,

27 + 27 × 27 − 27 ÷ 27 = −701

Interchanging the signs,

27 + 27 ÷ 27 - 27 × 27 = - 701

Using BODMAS rule,

27 + 1 – 27 × 27 = - 701

28 – 729 = - 701

-701 = - 701

Hence, option 4 is the correct answer

questions.question: Which part protects an unopened flower?

• **Sepals** protect an unopened flower

 
 
• Sepals are green, leaf-like structures that protect the flower in the **bud stage.**
 
• Sepals are collectively called the **calyx.**
 
• Sepals most resemble leaves due to their green color.
 
• Sepals may be brightly colored and function as petals when true petals are missing.
 
 
• **Virgin’s bower and the Bougainvillea **are examples of Sepals functioned as petals.
 
 
 
• The number of petals will be the same as the number of sepals in most cases.

• **Sachidananda Sinha** was appointed as the temporary chairman during its first meeting.
 
• **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** was elected as the permanent president of the constituent assembly on** December 11, 1946**.
 
• The Constituent Assembly also appointed** H.C. Mukherjee** as its vice president.
 
• The constitutional advisor to the constituent assembly was **B. N. Rao**.
